{{Short description|Norwegian biologist}}

'''Kjetill Sigurd Jakobsen''' is a Norwegian biologist. He is a professor at the Centre for Ecological and Evolutionary Synthesis (CEES) at the [[University of Oslo]] and a member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=University of Oslo|title=Kjetill Sigurd Jakobsen's official profile page|url=https://www.mn.uio.no/cees/english/people/chair/kjetillj/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=The Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters |title=Members of The Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters|url=https://dnva.no/medlemmer/15}}</ref>

Jakobsen is known for sequencing the [[Atlantic cod]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Titan.uio.no|title=Norwegian evolutionary biologists pushed the frontiers in international science|url=https://www.titan.uio.no/english/2018/norwegian-evolutionary-biologists-pushed-frontiers-international-science.html}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=The genome sequence of Atlantic cod Jakobsen is also known for his contributions to protist evolution research,<ref>Refer to the following topics and Jakobsen's publications listed under them: [[SAR supergroup]], [[Kingdom_(biology)|Kingdom (biology)]], [[Telonemia]], [[Holozoa]], [[Capsaspora|''Capsaspora'']], [[Chromalveolate]], [[Breviata|''Breviata'']], [[Rhizaria]], [[Centrohelid]], [[Ochrophyte]], [[Chloroplast]], and [[Lepidodinium|''Lepidodinium'']].</ref> to the complex evolutionary processes of polyploids,<ref>Refer to the following topic and Jakobsen's publications listed under it: [[Viola_(plant)|Viola (plant)]].</ref> and toxin genes in cyanobacteria and dinoflagellates.<ref>Refer to the following topics and Jakobsen's publications listed under them: [[Cyanopeptolin]] and [[Dinotoxin]].</ref> Since 2018, Jakobsen has contributed to research on ''De novo'' gene birth<ref>Refer to the following topic and Jakobsen's publications listed under it: [[De novo gene birth|''De novo'' gene birth]].</ref> and Deep sea fish.<ref>Refer to the following topic and Jakobsen's publications listed under it: [[Deep sea fish]].</ref>
